translation: The Blessed Lord said: I shall unfold to you once more the absolute supreme apex of all theoretical wisdom (Jnanam). Mastering this science, all the ancient reflective sages successfully climbed out of human limitations and secured the highest perfection.

Taking firm refuge in this wisdom, they achieve a state of spiritual unity that matches My divine nature (mama sadharmyam-agatah). They are not forced into rebirth during the dawn of cosmic creation, nor are they disrupted or shaken during the hours of universal dissolution.

Primordial material nature in its entirety (Mahat Brahma) serves as My cosmic womb; within that field do I deposit the seed of consciousness, O descendant of Bharata! From that fundamental contact emerges the generation of all living creatures.

Across whatever biological wombs structural physical forms are brought forth, O son of Kunti, material nature is their collective, maternal womb, and I am the procreative, seed- bestowing Father (bi-japradah pita).

Sattva (purity, balance), Rajas (passionate restlessness), and Tamas (dark inertia)—these three internal modes born of material nature bind down the immutable, embodied spirit within the physical body, O mighty-armed warrior.

Of these, Sattva, owing to its pristine purity, is luminous and healthy. But look closely at its subtle trap, O sinless one: it binds the practitioner by creating a hidden attachment to intellectual pleasure (sukha-sangena) and bookish knowledge (jnana-sangena).
simple_explanation: Krishna warns that even a highly virtuous quality can become a binding trap if it breeds pride. If an intellectual scholar becomes so attached to his quiet study room that he refuses to step out and handle his messy social duties during a national crisis, his attachment to "intellectual peace" has become a block to his spiritual progress.

translation: Know that Rajas is passionate by nature, originating directly from burning longing and emotional infatuation (trishna-sanga-samudbhavam). It tightly shackles the embodied soul, O son of Kunti, by engineering an obsessive attachment to reward-driven labor and material achievements.

But know that Tamas is born of absolute ignorance, acting as the prime cause for the blind delusion of all embodied beings, O descendant of Bharata! It shackles the human consciousness through reckless confusion (pramada), chronic laziness (alasya), and excessive stupor or sleep (nidra).

Sattva anchors the mind in internal contentment; Rajas hitches the awareness to endless material work; while Tamas, completely covering over the discriminating intellect, hitches the life to reckless errors and delusion, O Bharata.

Sometimes Sattva emerges dominant by crushing down Rajas and Tamas, O Bharata. At other times, Rajas surges ahead by overriding Sattva and Tamas; and similarly, Tamas takes over by smothering Sattva and Rajas.
When the light of clear discernment and intelligence radiates out through all the sensory gateways of this physical body, then you should understand that Sattva is dominant.

Greed, restless outbound movement, starting multiple commercial projects, inability to calm the thoughts, and constant longing—these traits burst forth when Rajas is dominant, O foremost of the Bharata dynasty!
Mental darkness, complete inertia, reckless confusion, and absolute delusion—these traits freeze the life when Tamas is dominant, O joy of the Kuru clan!
If an embodied soul exits the physical body when Sattva is dominant, he ascends straight to the pure, untainted realms of the highest knowers of reality.

Exiting the body when Rajas is dominant, he is reborn among those who are intensely attached to reward-driven labor. Similarly, dying when Tamas is dominant, he is reborn within the dull-witted environments of the heavily deluded.
The consequence of a pure, righteous action is declared to be Sattvic and clean. While the consequence of Rajas is future sorrow (dukham), and the consequence of Tamas is deep, stultifying ignorance.
From Sattva emerges direct wisdom; from Rajas springs greed; while from Tamas comes reckless confusion, blind delusion, and dense ignorance.

Those anchored in Sattva ascend upward to higher evolutionary tracks; those dominated by Rajas stay suspended in the middle zones; while those trapped within the degrading habits of Tamas slide downward into misery.

When an enlightened observer directly perceives that there is absolutely no independent author of action operating across nature besides these three modes, and tracks that which stands supreme beyond these qualities—he attains My divine nature.

Rising completely above these three modes of nature that have generated his physical body, the embodied soul, fully liberated from the grip of birth, death, decay, and suffering, tastes the nectar of immortality (amritam-ashnute).

Arjuna said: What are the concrete psychological markers of one who has successfully crossed beyond these three modes of nature, O Lord? What is his conduct in real life, and how does he dissolve the grip of these three properties?

The Blessed Lord said: He who does not hate illumination (Sattva), active movement (办事), or temporary confusion (Tamas) when they spontaneously surge up inside his nervous system, nor craves after them when they recede;
simple_explanation: Krishna defines the supreme standard of a master mind (Gunatita). A master mind does not waste energy picking fights with his biology. If a wave of fatigue (Tamas) or sudden ambition (Rajas) passes through his brain due to bad weather or diet, he tracks it with detachment, refusing to let it alter his core purpose. He treats them as passing weather outside his window.

translation: He who sits detached like an unconcerned onlooker, remaining entirely undisturbed by the modes of nature; who rests secure, realizing that "it is merely the qualities interacting with their corresponding properties," and never wavers;

Completely balanced in pleasure and pain, anchored securely within his own selfhood (svasthah), evaluating a clod of earth, a stone, and gold as equal, unswerving under pleasant or unpleasant turns of fortune, a wise sage of steel fortitude (dhira), remaining even-minded under fierce slander or lavish praise;

Impartial under public honor or stinging disgrace, identical toward the factions of a companion or an adversary, and who has thoroughly cast off the instinct for reward-driven undertakings—he is definitively called a master who has crossed beyond the modes of nature (Gunatita).

And he who serves Me with unswerving, single-minded devotional practice (bhakti-yogena), breaks completely through the chains of these three modes of nature and becomes fully qualified to merge into Absolute Brahman (Brahma-bhuyaya kalpate).

For I am the absolute Ground and foundation upon which rests the immortal, changeless Brahman, the eternal cosmic righteousness (shashvatasya dharmasya), and the infinite, absolute Bliss that never fades.
